title: Find the First F
description: Play the leftmost F3 key five times, releasing it between notes.
hint: The far-left white key is F3. Tap the highlighted first key.
spokenInstructions: Hey Cleo, for this lesson we are going to play the leftmost f3 key five times, releasing it between notes. Let's find F three. It's the white key on the far left of your little piano. Watch it glow yellow. Press that key five times, lifting your finger between each press. Listen for a happy chime when you get it right!

title: Five-Finger Walk
description: Walk from F3 to C4 and back, one note at a time.
hint: Play F3, G3, A3, B♭3, C4, then back to F3.
spokenInstructions: Hey Cleo, for this lesson we are going to walk from f3 to c4 and back, one note at a time. Time for a five-finger walk! We will play F three, G three, A three, B flat three, and C four. Then we'll walk back down. Watch the glowing key and play just one note at a time. The B flat key is black. You can go as slowly as you like!

title: A Little Melody
description: Try a short tune using keys in the first octave of your toy piano.
hint: Find the highlighted key and play each note in turn.
spokenInstructions: Hey Cleo, for this lesson we are going to try a short tune using keys in the first octave of your toy piano. play a little melody! Follow the yellow key as it changes. Sometimes we play the same note twice. When that happens, lift your finger and play it again. Listen to the next note if you need help. Ready? Let's make music!

title: High and Low F
description: Hear and play F in three different registers on your toy piano.
hint: Play the leftmost F3, F4 in the middle, and rightmost F5.
spokenInstructions: Hey Cleo, for this lesson we are going to hear and play f in three different registers on your toy piano. explore high and low sounds! Begin with F three, the white key at the far left. Then find F four, one octave higher, and F five, at the far right. Play F four again, and finish on F three. Can you hear the difference?

title: Twinkle Twinkle Little Star
description: Play Twinkle Twinkle and the beginning of its next phrase. A gentle beginner excerpt in F major.
hint: Start on F4 (the middle F); follow the gold notes. B♭4 is a black key.
spokenInstructions: Hey Cleo, for this lesson we are going to play twinkle twinkle and the beginning of its next phrase. a gentle beginner excerpt in f major. play Twinkle Twinkle Little Star! Start with the F key near the middle of your piano. Play each glowing note one at a time. First, tap Hear whole melody so you know how the tune sounds. Then follow the golden keys. Some notes repeat, so lift your finger between them. Take your time!

title: Wheels on the Bus · Traditional Tune
description: Play an easy instrumental passage using the old Mulberry Bush melody commonly sung with Wheels on the Bus.
hint: Start on C5. The melody repeats notes and moves by small steps.
spokenInstructions: Hey Cleo, for this lesson we are going to play an easy instrumental passage using the old mulberry bush melody commonly sung with wheels on the bus. go for a musical bus ride! This lesson uses a traditional tune often sung with The Wheels on the Bus. Listen to the whole melody first, then find C five and play along with the glowing keys. Keep the short repeated notes light and bouncy. You can go at your own speed!

title: Puppy Rescue Parade · Original

hint: Begin on F4 and follow the rising notes, then play the little descending phrase.
spokenInstructions: Hey Cleo, for this lesson we are going to an original adventure melody for rescue-pup fans. this is not the television show's theme music. Calling all rescue puppies! Let's play a brand new puppy rescue melody. It has a bouncy, brave sound, and it is our own tune, not the Paw Patrol television theme. Hear the full melody, then follow the golden keys. Can you make it to the end of the rescue mission?

Listen to the whole melody, then follow the notes on your piano. This one has a bouncy rhythm!

title: Mary Had a Little Lamb
description: A short, traditional beginner melody. Practice stepping down and up between neighbouring keys.

spokenInstructions: Hey Cleo, for this lesson we are going to a short, traditional beginner melody. practice stepping down and up between neighbouring keys. play Mary Had a Little Lamb! title: Two Notes Together
description: Find a simple fifth: F3 and C4. Build both notes to complete each chord.
hint: Play F3 and C4 together; both keys glow gold.
spokenInstructions: Hey Cleo, for this lesson we are going to find a simple fifth: f3 and c4. build both notes to complete each chord. A chord can have two or more notes. First let us try an F and C together. Touch both golden keys. With a microphone, you can play the notes one at a time in build mode. With MIDI, try pressing them together.

title: Happy and Moody Thirds

hint: First F3 and A3, then F3 and A-flat 3.
spokenInstructions: Hey Cleo, for this lesson we are going to hear a major third and a minor third. notice the one-key difference. Our two-note friends can sound happy or moody. Play F with A, then F with A flat. Watch how changing one key changes the sound.

title: Major or Minor?

hint: First F–A–C, then F–A♭–C.
spokenInstructions: Hey Cleo, for this lesson we are going to compare f major with f minor by lowering a3 to a♭3. Major and minor chords can feel different. Play F major with A, then F minor with A flat. Only one key changes!

spokenInstructions: Hey Cleo, for this lesson we are going to play the familiar f–b♭–c progression. Three chords can make a whole song. Play F major, B flat major, C major, then back home to F.

title: Broken Chord, Full Chord

spokenInstructions: Hey Cleo, for this lesson we are going to first play f3, a3 and c4 one at a time; then play them together. Sometimes we play a chord one note at a time. That is called a broken chord. Now let us try all three together!
